context_overflow.note: Context-pressure text followed by shorter reasoning or more errors - degradation under pressure, not content dropped and acted on as if present. Not exact.

delegation_failure.note: Fires only when a delegation-marker tool returns an error-like result. AF-0071 also covers brief distortion and discarded results, so it is broader.

early_abort.note: Fires on 0 < step_count < 3; does not require a completion claim.

environment_drift.note: Detector is 'environment-style errors (timeout, click_fail, not_found) dominate' - a proxy for the described 'page changed underneath the runner'.

memory_overload.note: Context usage >= 85% plus degradation evidence; this is the category that can carry AF-0064's eviction/compaction counters. Near-synonym of context_overflow by design.

model_limit.note: Detector is step_count > 50 and < 2 URLs - the stuck_loop test at a higher threshold. An Agent-Xray AF-0125/AF-0058 split is partly a step-count artefact.

prompt_bug.note: Confusion/uncertainty regex in reasoning; also the fallback when nothing else matches but a prompt-section pattern does. Harness prompt quality rather than user-request ambiguity.

reasoning_bug.note: errors == 0, > 1 tool, > 1 URL, still failed - effectively 'progressed cleanly with no hard signal'. Broad by design.

routing_bug.note: GAP: fires when a step's exposed tool list is EMPTY - the harness never scoped the tool in. Shares AF-0007's symptom at the harness layer; no AF mode for tool-not-exposed yet.

spin.note: Longest consecutive streak of the same tool name >= 5 - AF-0058's first symptom nearly verbatim. Third in the cascade, so it wins over stuck_loop when both fire.

stuck_loop.note: unique_urls <= 1 and step_count >= 5. No repetition required - absence of navigation progress. Same test as model_limit at a lower threshold.

timeout.note: Step budget (>= 40) plus a stalled final window; no elapsed-time signal. AF-0136 covers time or step budgets, hence exact; the stall requirement overlaps AF-0058.

tool_bug.note: Intended meaning (right tool, bad result) is AF-0149, which this category prompted. As detected it fires when unknown_tool + validation + other errors dominate, so it also captures fabricated tools (AF-0011) and schema errors (AF-0023); and its error-only signal misses AF-0149's soft-error cases. Hence overlaps x3, no exact.

tool_rejection_mismatch.note: Non-expected tool rejections on >= 30% of steps.

tool_selection_bug.note: Right tool available, agent used something else (search-only when browser exposed; or one tool across many URLs). No invocation error involved. This category, with Model-or-Harness 'Incorrect Tool Selection', is why AF-0157 exists.

F1.1 Tool or Action Planning Error.note: Wrong tool or action chosen for the step (7 cases).

F1.2 Response Format Error.note: A node's output does not match the format the next node expects (28). AF-0023 is the closest - the invalid-invocation shape seen from the consumer side. No AF mode for malformed inter-node output specifically.

F1.3 Response Content Deviation.note: Content does not meet the instruction (47). The paper pairs it with F1.5 under 'response misalignments'; instruction-following shape.

F1.4 Knowledge or Reasoning Limitation.note: Most frequent root cause (55); repair = model upgrade or augmentation - AF-0125's third symptom.

F1.5 Poor Prompt Design.note: GAP: second most frequent (52). Harness prompt quality as a root cause - the same thing Agent-Xray's prompt_bug names. Cause-level rather than symptom-level, so it may not belong in a symptom registry at all; recorded as a gap to decide, not to fill by default.

F1.6 Language or Encoding Issue.note: Wrong language or character encoding in a node's output (15). No AF mode; borderline in scope.

F1.7 Tool Invocation or KB Retrieval Err.note: Tool call fails or knowledge-base lookup returns wrong/nothing (9).

F2.1 Missing Input Verification.note: Workflow passes unchecked input between nodes (15); a node proceeds on a value it should have validated.

F2.2 Unreasonable Node Dependency.note: Dependencies between workflow nodes wired wrongly (17).

F2.3 Loops and Deadlocks.note: Workflow-structure loop or deadlock (3); the repetition is in the orchestration graph, not the agent's reasoning.

F2.4 Faulty Conditional Judgment.note: Branching condition routes to the wrong path (11).

F2.5 Improper Task Decomposition.note: Sub-tasks scoped wrongly (6) - AF-0071's incomplete/distorted brief.

F2.7 Cross-agent tool or interface misma.note: Interface between agents/tools does not line up (11).

F3.1 Network and Resource Fluctuation.note: Transient network or resource trouble (13). AF-0170 covers any upstream failure, so broader.

F3.2 Service Unavailability.note: External service down (10). AF-0170 also covers a live service failing a request, so broader.

Agent Lifecycle and State.note: 38. Scheduling, delegation logic, state transitions, termination logic. Runtime face: skipped tasks, repeated actions, lost intermediate state, uncontrolled loops, failure to stop.

Dependency and Environment Management.note: 72 - the largest category. Dependency resolution, installation, upstream breaking changes. Out of scope.

External Access.note: 19. Invalid endpoints, connection settings, credentials, permissions. Runtime face: unreachable service (AF-0170), credential invalidated mid-run (AF-0118).

Failure Handling & Implementation Robust.note: 47. Suppressed exceptions, mis-propagated errors, broken recovery. Runtime face: silent failures and the system continuing on erroneous state - the harness-side cause of what a trajectory shows as AF-0042 / AF-0149.

Input Interpretation.note: 59. Parsing, validation, encoding and type-assumption bugs in pipeline code. Framework defect; out of scope. (Its 'Data Schema Mismatch' root cause is the same shape as AgentFail F1.2.)

LLM Interaction Faults.note: 48. Model/provider misconfiguration, incompatible API usage, token accounting, context-window handling. Runtime face: context overflow / truncated prompts (AF-0064), unintended or redundant tool invocation (AF-0166), rejected API calls.

Memory Management.note: 8. Serialization, timestamps, persistent-storage bugs in the memory implementation. Framework defect; not a trajectory-observable agent failure.

Resource Interaction.note: 21. Invalid paths, filesystem assumptions, storage/database misconfiguration. Framework/config defect; out of scope.

System Coordination.note: 6. Race conditions in concurrent/streaming execution. Out of scope.

Tool Invocation.note: 11. Defective tool, or tool invoked against its API contract (unsupported args, malformed request). Both sides of the AF-0023 / AF-0149 line.

User Interface Defects.note: 13. Dashboards misrepresenting state. Out of scope.

Guardrails Triggered.note: GAP: the category is an RAI/safety-policy refusal OR an external site access restriction (CAPTCHA, login wall, 403, paywall, robots.txt). AF-0095 is the harness's own policy/approval gate and covers the first half; the external-access block is environment-layer and has no AF mode. Magentic's 9/44 here are a mix of Azure RAI filters and Cloudflare/CAPTCHA.

Inconclusive.note: Residual label, not a failure mode. The judge must supply a free-text custom_category with it, so AgentRx output can carry labels outside the ten.

Instruction/Plan Adherence Failure.note: Goal is correct (checklist Q1 excludes wrong-problem cases) but a step required by the plan, domain policy or orchestrator was skipped, reordered or padded with unneeded actions. AF splits it: under-execution (AF-0153, with stopping early AF-0077 as its own mode) and over-execution (AF-0166). The most common failure event in AgentRx's own annotations; this category is one of the sources for AF-0153 and AF-0166.

Intent Not Supported.note: Requested action needs a capability no available tool provides. In multi-agent runs the requester is often the orchestrator (FileSurfer asked to listen to audio) - same shape one level down.

Intent-Plan Misalignment.note: Wrong objective or key constraint violated because intent was misunderstood; checklist excludes missing-information and tool-error causes.

Invalid Invocation.note: Explicit parse/validation/schema/syntax error for a concrete call; checklist excludes infra and access-block causes.

Invention of New Information.note: Fabricated facts and hallucinated state ('download succeeded') are AF-0161; fabricated tool/parameter schemas are AF-0011. The category also covers unjustified OMISSION of relevant information, which neither mode does - hence narrower, not exact. One of the sources for AF-0161.

Misinterpretation of Tool Output.note: Judge name is 'Misinterpretation of Tool Output / Handoff Failure': reasoning that contradicts, omits part of, or miscomputes from the agent's OWN OR ANOTHER AGENT's output. AF-0042 is the own-tool-output slice; a parent misusing a sub-agent's result is AF-0071's third symptom. 15/44 Magentic root causes are orchestrator-misreads-WebSurfer.

System Failure.note: Explicit infra/connectivity signal during a tool call - timeout, connection refused, DNS failure, endpoint unreachable, service unavailable, premature termination. AF splits it by mechanism: upstream service failure (AF-0170, listed first), time/step budget, rate-limit cascade, tool-internal error. 'Premature termination' of the run itself is the residue none of them names. Context truncation is not in the definition and is not mapped here. One of the sources for AF-0170.

Underspecified User Intent.note: A specific required piece of information is absent from all evidence and the agent proceeded without it or failed to ask. AF-0103 describes the same failure from the 'picked a reading silently' side.

Communication Failure (peer).note: Peers fail to exchange needed information.

Communication Failure (subagent).note: Orchestrator omits context, fails to route, or fails to use the sub-agent's output; or the sub-agent fails to report. AF-0071's first and third clauses.

Context Rationale Erosion.note: Harness compaction keeps an instruction's surface action but drops its rationale; the model, working from the lossy summary, reverses a decision it had honoured. AF-0064's summarisation case exactly; attributed to the harness when compaction is harness-driven, as AFR does.

Contextual Sycophancy.note: GAP: adopts the views of third-party content it is analysing. No AF mode; single source.

Delegation Failure (peer).note: Peers fail to coordinate division of work and dependencies. AF-0071 is orchestrator-shaped; peer coordination is adjacent.

Delegation Failure (subagent).note: Orchestrator assigns work with wrong scope or dependencies - AF-0071's first clause; AF-0071 also covers the result side.

Domain Knowledge Deficit.note: One of AF-0125's named dimensions (domain knowledge).

Evaluation Awareness.note: Behaviour change on inferring it is being evaluated; the paper notes it may be 'detectable only via internal activations'. Fails AFR's trajectory-observability bar; not marked GAP.

Goal Drift.note: GAP: recent context displaces the original instruction over a long run. Distinct mechanism (recency); ends up looking like AF-0088 late in the trajectory.

Incorrect Tool Selection.note: 'Selects a tool that is completely wrong for the task or fundamentally inefficient.'

Indirect Prompt Injection.note: GAP: directives in third-party content treated as owner instructions. Security-shaped; no AF mode.

Instruction-Following Failure.note: Ignores parts of the spec, partially completes, or violates explicit constraints (time, call or token limits). AF-0153 and AF-0077 are each one slice.

Instruction-Grader Mismatch.note: Owner-side: instruction differs from the owner's real intent as the grader captures it; the agent follows the instruction and is judged against the intent. Not an agent fault; AF-0103 is the nearest shape.

Malformed Arguments.note: Call does not fit the tool's schema; immediate exception.

Memory Following Failure.note: GAP: memory read and then ignored. No AF mode.

Memory Rationale Erosion.note: GAP: memory written without the reasoning behind it, later reversed. Memory twin of Context Rationale Erosion; no AF mode.

Missed Read.note: GAP: memory holds the fact; model does not consult it. No AF mode.

Missed Write.note: GAP: relevant fact not stored to durable memory. AFR has no memory modes; single source.

Mistranslation.note: Tool-side: the integration layer garbles an observation or mis-maps the action. One kind of AF-0149; the paper's only tool-side fault.

Observation Failure.note: A cue present in the observation space is overlooked and the model acts without resolving the ambiguity it would have settled.

Over-initiative.note: GAP: consequential action taken where a clarifying question was due, or information volunteered unasked. Acting-beyond-scope has no AF mode; the clarify-first half is AF-0103, the surplus-action half AF-0166.

Overgeneralization.note: GAP: one-off workaround stored as a permanent rule. Memory; no AF mode.

Pollution.note: GAP: transient logs dumped into durable memory. No AF mode.

Reasoning Failure.note: 'Fundamentally incapable of reasoning through the problem; flawed plan; logical error.'

Recovery Failure (external environment).note: GAP: the environment problem was recoverable and the model gave up or acted on a false assumption instead of retrying, diagnosing, routing around or asking. Failure-to-recover has no AF mode.

Recovery Failure (local environment).note: GAP: same definition as the external-environment variant, for local conditions (missing file, broken state).

Redundancy.note: GAP: same information written repeatedly to memory. No AF mode.

Satisficing.note: 'Declares the job done while real work remains undone or only stubbed in' - AF-0077 to the letter; the paper adds the motive (effort minimisation), which AFR does not record. 'Stops at the first result that clears a low bar' overlaps AF-0086.

Service Failure.note: External service hits an internal error, timeout or rate limit and fails the request outright, unrecoverably. The rate-limit case is AF-0130's trigger.

Specification Gaming.note: GAP: exploiting the reward/grading channel. AF-0088's 'optimises a proxy objective not requested' is the honest-mistake version; deliberate gaming has no mode.

Stale State Delivery.note: GAP: service returns a healthy status but stale data, with no freshness signal. AF-0118 is 'the world changed'; this is 'the service lied about freshness'. No exact AF mode.

State Staleness.note: GAP: stored memory not updated when the world changes. AF-0118 is the environment-side cousin.

State Tracking Failure.note: 'Trapped in a repetitive execution cycle ... fails to recognize its repeated steps are no longer making progress' - AF-0058. Test loops and re-reads are its named sub-cases. The paper puts this on the MODEL side; AFR's layer is harness - see notes.

Suboptimal Arguments.note: GAP: structurally valid but low-signal arguments (vague phrase into grep). Near AF-0023 but not invalid; no AF mode.

Sycophancy.note: GAP: output tailored to agree with the user over truth. No AF mode; single source so far.

Tool Feedback Neglect.note: Fails to act on an explicit signal in the tool response - the 'error field not acknowledged' slice of AF-0042.

Tool Hallucination.note: Calls a tool absent from the declared schema; immediate crash.

Tool Recovery Failure.note: GAP: after a tool anomaly (503, rate-limit, corrupted data) the model either retries futilely or over-trusts the broken data instead of pivoting. Failure-to-recover has no AF mode; this paper names it three times across edges.

Unauthorized Irreversible Action.note: GAP: high or infinite rollback-cost action taken without a mandatory human confirmation gate. No AF mode; the inverse of AF-0095.

Under-initiative.note: GAP: halting, over-deferring, or demanding confirmation the task did not need. The halting half is AF-0077; over-deferral has no AF mode.

Value Misalignment.note: Flawed ethical deliberation even when the action is right. Out of AFR's trajectory-symptom scope; not marked GAP.

Output-Fabrication.note: Tool called; answer adds invented structured information not present in the return. AF-0161 covers fabricated content in general, so it is broader.

Result-Ignore.note: Tool called; final answer omits the returned value (typically in favour of the memorised prior). The ignore-in-favour-of-prior slice of AF-0042, which also covers misinterpretation.

Tool-Skip.note: No valid executed tool call on a tool-required task; includes answers written in a tool-style format with no call behind them (App. D.1). AF-0153 covers any prescribed step left out, so it is broader. The tool-style-answer variant also brushes AF-0161.

Unnecessary-Tool-Use.note: Control task (no tool needed) answered with a tool call anyway. The one-extra-call slice of AF-0166. Rare label; judge kappa 0.23 but raw agreement 0.95.

Wrong-Answer.note: Control task answered directly and incorrectly - a parametric knowledge error, not a tool-use failure. Left unmapped on purpose; AF-0125 would overstate it.

modes.description: The user's goal is coherent and well specified, but lies outside what the agent's tool set or permissions can accomplish. The agent proceeds anyway instead of reporting the gap.
discriminators: vs AF-0103: the intent here is clear, not underspecified
vs AF-0095: nothing blocked the agent; the capability was simply absent
vs AF-0077: the capability was absent; the agent did not stop short of work it could have done
symptoms: no available tool covers the requested capability
agent substitutes a partial or adjacent action without saying so
final response claims completion of an action never performed
modes.title: Intent not supported

modes.description: The agent invents a tool, parameter, endpoint or field that does not exist in the provided schema, and calls it as though it did.
discriminators: vs AF-0023: the tool exists here only in the model's output, not in the schema
vs AF-0042: the fabrication is in the call, not in reading the result
vs AF-0149: the tool does not exist; an existing tool that misbehaves is AF-0149
vs AF-0157: the tool does not exist; in AF-0157 an existing, wrong tool was chosen
vs AF-0161: fabrication is in the tool or parameter name at call time, not in content or claims
symptoms: tool name absent from the advertised tool list
parameter key absent from the tool's schema
invocation rejected by the harness as unknown
modes.title: Fabricated tool signature

modes.description: The agent calls a tool that genuinely exists but with arguments that violate its schema — wrong types, missing required fields, malformed structure, or a call made in an invalid state.
discriminators: vs AF-0011: the tool and parameters exist; only the values are wrong
vs AF-0088: the tool choice is appropriate for the plan; the call itself is malformed
vs AF-0042: the call itself is malformed or rejected; nothing was misread downstream
vs AF-0149: the call itself violates the schema; a schema-valid call that fails inside the tool is AF-0149
vs AF-0157: the call is malformed; in AF-0157 the call is valid and the tool is the wrong choice
symptoms: schema validation error returned by the harness
required parameter absent or null
argument type mismatch against the declared schema
modes.title: Invalid tool invocation

modes.description: The tool returned correct output and the agent drew a conclusion the output does not support — inverting a boolean, missing an error field, reading a truncated result as complete.
discriminators: vs AF-0023: the call succeeded; the failure is in interpretation
vs AF-0011: nothing was invented at call time
vs AF-0086: enough was read; what was read was misinterpreted
vs AF-0149: the output was correct and misread; an incorrect or unusable output is AF-0149
vs AF-0161: a real output was misread; in AF-0161 content was added that no output supports
symptoms: agent's stated conclusion contradicts the returned payload
error field present in output but not acknowledged
downstream steps proceed on a value not present in the result
modes.title: Tool output misread

modes.description: In a code-editing workflow, the agent repeatedly edits and re-runs a failing test without the failure signal changing, making no progress toward a fix.
discriminators: vs AF-0058: repetition here is scoped to an edit/verify cycle with a test oracle
vs AF-0125: the task is within capability; the loop is procedural
symptoms: identical test failure output across three or more cycles
edits revert or oscillate between the same two states
no new diagnostic information gathered between attempts
modes.title: Test failure loop

modes.description: The agent retries the same action, or cycles a small set of actions, without the environment state or its own information changing between attempts.
discriminators: vs AF-0142: repetition here is of actions, not of reads
vs AF-0049: not scoped to a test/verify cycle
vs AF-0095: no policy or approval event in the trace; the repetition is unprompted
vs AF-0125: attempts are identical, not varied failing approaches
vs AF-0130: no quota or 429 errors in the trace; the repetition originates in the agent
vs AF-0166: the same action repeated, not a superfluous distinct one
symptoms: identical action repeated with identical arguments
step count grows while observable state is unchanged
no new information enters context between attempts
modes.title: Unproductive repetition

modes.description: Content the agent needs is silently dropped from context by window management — truncation, eviction, or summarisation — and the agent proceeds as though it were still present.
discriminators: vs AF-0142: content is genuinely gone here, not present-but-re-read
vs AF-0125: a window-management failure, not a capability ceiling
symptoms: reference to content no longer in the window
harness truncation or eviction event in the trace
agent re-derives a fact it had already established
modes.title: Context overflow truncation

modes.description: A sub-agent or delegated call is dispatched with an incomplete or distorted brief, returns a result the parent cannot use, or its result is discarded without being incorporated.
discriminators: vs AF-0088: the parent's plan is sound; the loss happens at the delegation boundary
vs AF-0086: information was gathered but not transferred
symptoms: sub-agent brief omits constraints present in the parent task
sub-agent result not referenced in subsequent parent steps
parent re-does work the sub-agent already completed
modes.title: Delegation failure

modes.description: The agent stops and reports completion while parts of the requested task remain undone, unverified, or explicitly deferred.
discriminators: vs AF-0007: the work was possible with available tools
vs AF-0095: nothing blocked the agent from continuing
vs AF-0086: sub-goals are left undone; the issue is stopping, not thin evidence behind a conclusion
vs AF-0136: the agent chose to stop; no external deadline cut it off
vs AF-0153: the agent stopped; in AF-0153 it continued past the missing step
symptoms: final response claims done with open sub-goals in the plan
verification step named in the plan never executed
agent asks no clarifying question yet stops short
modes.title: Premature termination

modes.description: The agent commits to a conclusion on evidence too thin to support it, without gathering readily available additional sources.
discriminators: vs AF-0042: the sources read were interpreted correctly, there were just too few
vs AF-0077: the agent did not stop early; it concluded early
vs AF-0071: no sub-agent is involved; evidence was never gathered rather than gathered and dropped
vs AF-0153: too little evidence behind a conclusion, not a prescribed step left out
vs AF-0161: the claim is under-sourced, not invented; AF-0161 has no support at all
symptoms: single source underpins a load-bearing claim
available search or read tools left unused
confidence in the final answer not matched by evidence in the trace
modes.title: Insufficient sources

modes.description: The agent constructs a plan, or routes to a sub-task, that does not serve the user's actual goal — solving an adjacent or reformulated problem instead.
discriminators: vs AF-0103: the intent was clear enough to plan against
vs AF-0023: the plan is wrong, not the mechanics of a call
vs AF-0071: the plan itself is wrong; nothing is lost at a delegation boundary
vs AF-0153: the plan itself is wrong; AF-0153 has the right plan with one prescribed step missing
vs AF-0157: the goal is wrong; AF-0157 has the right goal and the wrong instrument for a step
vs AF-0166: the plan serves the wrong goal; AF-0166 serves the right goal with a surplus action
symptoms: plan steps do not map onto stated goal criteria
agent optimises a proxy objective not requested
successful execution of the wrong task
modes.title: Plan/intent misalignment

modes.description: A policy, approval gate, or safety filter halts the agent, and the agent neither surfaces the block clearly nor adapts its approach around it.
discriminators: vs AF-0007: the capability exists; policy withheld it
vs AF-0058: retries follow a block rather than a null result
vs AF-0077: a block event precedes the stop; the halt is imposed, not chosen
symptoms: approval or policy rejection event in the trace
agent retries the blocked action unchanged
block not reported in the final response
modes.title: Guardrail block

modes.description: The request admits several materially different readings and the agent picks one silently, without flagging the ambiguity or asking.
discriminators: vs AF-0088: ambiguity originates upstream of the plan
vs AF-0007: the request may be entirely achievable once disambiguated
symptoms: multiple defensible interpretations of the request
agent's chosen reading never stated to the user
no clarifying question despite a consequential fork
modes.title: Underspecified intent

modes.description: The environment changes underneath the agent mid-run — file contents, credentials, service versions, network state — and the agent continues acting on a stale model of it.
discriminators: vs AF-0142: the content genuinely changed here
vs AF-0130: drift is in state, not in throughput limits
vs AF-0149: the environment changed underneath the agent; a tool that fails against unchanged state is AF-0149
vs AF-0170: the target changed state; in AF-0170 it is unavailable
symptoms: read value differs from a previously read value with no agent write between
credential or session invalidated mid-run
dependency or service version changes between steps
modes.title: Environment drift

modes.description: The task exceeds what the underlying model can do at all — reasoning depth, context length, domain knowledge — rather than failing on procedure or tooling.
discriminators: vs AF-0058: attempts vary rather than repeat
vs AF-0064: not a window-management artefact
vs AF-0049: attempts differ qualitatively; not an edit/verify loop with an unchanging test signal
symptoms: repeated qualitatively different attempts, all failing
failure persists across harness changes
task succeeds when the model is upgraded, harness held constant
modes.title: Model capability limit

modes.description: A throughput or quota limit triggers retries which themselves consume quota, degrading the run beyond the original limit.
discriminators: vs AF-0058: repetition is driven by the limit, not by the agent's reasoning
vs AF-0136: quota exhaustion rather than a time or step ceiling
vs AF-0118: the environment's state is unchanged; only its quota is exhausted
vs AF-0170: throttling with a 429/quota pattern, not a service that is down or unreachable
symptoms: 429 or quota errors clustering in time
retry rate increasing rather than backing off
unrelated later steps failing on exhausted quota
modes.title: Rate limit cascade

modes.description: A step or the whole run exceeds an externally imposed budget — wall-clock time, or a maximum step / iteration count — and is cut off, leaving the task partially executed and the agent unaware of the boundary. The two budgets present identically in a trajectory, so they share a mode.
discriminators: vs AF-0130: a time or step ceiling, not a throughput quota; no 429-style errors
vs AF-0077: termination is external, not the agent's decision
vs AF-0170: the run's own budget was exhausted, not a single upstream call failing
symptoms: run or step terminated by an external time limit or step/iteration cap
no completion signal in the trace
partial writes or half-applied state left behind
modes.title: Time or step budget exhausted

modes.description: The agent re-reads a source it has already read within the same context window, with no intervening change to the target, and treats the result as new information.
discriminators: vs AF-0058: repetition here is of reads specifically, not action retries
vs AF-0064: context is not overflowing; the content is still present
vs AF-0118: the target genuinely did not change
symptoms: repeated identical read call within one context window
no intervening write to the read target
step count grows without state change
modes.title: Stale context re-read

modes.description: An existing tool, called with a schema-valid invocation, fails on its own account — raising an internal error, returning an empty, malformed or truncated payload, or reporting a result that contradicts the state it claims to describe. The call was right; the tool was not.
discriminators: vs AF-0023: the call passed validation; the failure originates inside the tool
vs AF-0011: the tool exists and was advertised; nothing was invented
vs AF-0042: the output was genuinely wrong or unusable, not merely misread
vs AF-0118: the same call against the same state fails; nothing in the environment changed between calls
vs AF-0161: the tool returned the bad value; in AF-0161 the agent produced it
vs AF-0170: the tool's own code or integration failed; in AF-0170 the tool ran and its upstream dependency failed
references: Agent-Xray `tool_bug` (https://github.com/GeeIHadAGoodTime/Agent-Xray/blob/main/src/agent_xray/root_cause.py) - the category that exposed the registry's empty tool layer
symptoms: schema-valid call returns an error originating inside the tool (internal exception, stack trace, 5xx)
tool returns an empty, malformed, or truncated payload for a well-formed request
tool reports success but the state it claims to have produced is not observed afterwards
an identical call succeeds later, or elsewhere, with no change to arguments or target state
modes.title: Tool defect

modes.description: Pursuing the correct goal, with the needed information available, the agent leaves out a step the task, plan, policy or specification required — a tool call, a confirmation, a check, a sub-task — and continues or concludes without it. The goal and the rest of the plan are right; one prescribed action is missing.
discriminators: vs AF-0088: the goal and plan are right; only a prescribed step is missing
vs AF-0077: the run continues past the omission; AF-0077 is omission by stopping
vs AF-0086: a prescribed step was skipped, not merely too little evidence gathered for a conclusion
vs AF-0157: nothing was done in the step's place; AF-0157 substitutes a wrong tool
vs AF-0166: something required is absent; AF-0166 is something unrequired present
symptoms: an action present in the reference sequence or mandated by policy is absent from the trace
a required confirmation, authentication or verification step does not precede the action it was meant to gate
an answer or completion is produced without the evidence or side-effect the omitted step would have provided
the stated goal and the surrounding plan are otherwise correct
modes.title: Required step omitted

modes.description: A tool fit for the step was available and advertised, and the agent invoked a different, less suitable one — functionally wrong or grossly inefficient — with a well-formed call, or worked around the needed tool with an inferior path. The call mechanics are fine; the choice is not.
discriminators: vs AF-0023: the calls are well-formed; the choice of tool is wrong
vs AF-0011: the tool used exists and was advertised
vs AF-0088: the goal and plan are right; the instrument for one step is wrong
vs AF-0153: something was done in the step - the wrong thing - rather than nothing
vs AF-0166: the step needed a tool; the wrong one was chosen, rather than a tool being used where none was needed
references: Model or Harness? 'Incorrect Tool Selection' - https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28802
AgentFail 'F1.1 Tool or Action Planning Error' - https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23735
symptoms: a tool suited to the step is in the advertised set and is not called
the tool that was called cannot produce what the step needs, or produces it at far higher cost
calls are schema-valid; no invocation error is raised
later steps compensate for the shortfall (re-query, manual parsing, guessing) or the result is degraded
modes.title: Wrong tool selected

modes.description: The agent introduces a fact, value, citation or claim about state that no input, context item or tool output supports — inventing a figure, asserting that a file was written or a step succeeded, or attributing a result to a tool that did not return it — and proceeds on it.
discriminators: vs AF-0011: the fabrication is in content or claims, not in a tool or parameter name at call time
vs AF-0042: no real output was misread; content was added that no output supports
vs AF-0149: the tool did not return the bad value; the agent produced it
vs AF-0086: the claim is ungrounded, not merely under-sourced
references: ToolFailBench 'Output-Fabrication' and tool-style answers without a call (App. D.1) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04686
symptoms: a value or claim in the agent's output is absent from every input, context item and tool result up to that step
a result is attributed to a tool that was not called or did not return it
a state change is asserted (file written, order placed, download complete) that later observation does not confirm
downstream steps rely on the invented claim
modes.title: Fabricated content

modes.description: The agent performs an action the task did not require and the plan did not need — a tool call, a side-effect, a sub-task — while the goal stays correct. The result may still be right; cost, latency or risk is incurred for nothing.
discriminators: vs AF-0058: a superfluous distinct action, not a repetition of the same one
vs AF-0088: goal and plan are right; one action is surplus
vs AF-0153: the inverse - something unrequired is present rather than something required absent
vs AF-0157: no tool was needed for the step at all, rather than the wrong one chosen for a needed step
symptoms: a tool call or step appears that the reference solution or control condition does not contain
the action's result is not used by any later step or by the final answer
the task is otherwise completed correctly
modes.title: Unnecessary action

modes.description: A remote service or endpoint the agent depends on — an API, a site, a model host, a database — fails the request on its own side: unreachable, DNS or connection refused, timed out, 5xx, declared unavailable. The call was well-formed and the local tool ran; what failed was upstream of it.
discriminators: vs AF-0149: the tool ran correctly; its upstream dependency failed
vs AF-0130: the service is down or unreachable, not throttling; no 429/quota pattern
vs AF-0136: a single upstream call timed out, rather than the run's own budget being exhausted
vs AF-0118: nothing about the target's state changed; it is unavailable
references: AgentFail 'F3.1 Network and Resource Fluctuation', 'F3.2 Service Unavailability' - https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23735
symptoms: connection, DNS, timeout or 5xx error naming a remote host or endpoint
the local tool wrapper executed; the failure is in the response from upstream
the same call later succeeds without change, or the service is independently reported down
the run halts or degrades at the dependent step
modes.title: External service failure

sources.name: Characterizing Faults in Agentic AI (fault-type taxonomy)
